Description: Alberto II della Scala, eldest son of Alboino I, ruled as Lord of Verona and Padua alongside his brother Mastino II. Gentle, cultured, and diplomatic, he managed civil administration and diplomatic chancelleries, maintaining economic stability during ceaseless foreign wars. Alberto II subsidized artists and scriptoriums across Verona and Padua, diffusing popular resentment over heavy military taxes through gracious and scholarly governance. Standing firm against Venetian armies, his diplomatic dexterity bought vital mobilization time, preserving river commerce across the Adige throughout grueling campaigns. Scholarly and gracious, Alberto II recognized that civic virtue healed the wounds of war, infusing Verona with luminous humanist culture during turbulent territorial campaigns. Throughout every bitter factional siege, imperial diet, and shifting territorial campaign across the Veneto, their relentless aristocratic dedication, strategic statecraft, chivalric discipline, steadfast valor, and immense personal resources preserve the sovereign dignity, mercantile wealth, and military supremacy of the Lordship of Verona, safeguarding civic liberty, territorial integrity, and Scaliger grandeur against every rival commune, hostile coalition, and Venetian league across northern Italy for future generations to inherit with pride, commanding profound imperial reverence from all subjects throughout Christendom and standing as an immortal beacon of chivalric honor and municipal liberty across European history.
Motivations: Stabilize Verona's home economy amidst the massive financial strains of Mastino II's wars.
Seek diplomatic mediation when Venice and Florence unite to crush Scaliger expansion.
Patronize artists and humanists to maintain Verona's reputation as a cultural capital.
Values: Believes compassionate administration commands deeper citizen loyalty than raw conquest.
Holds brotherly harmony supreme, curbing personal vanity to preserve united lordship.
Fears: Allied anti-Scaliger armies breaching the Adige to lay waste to Verona's civic treasures.
Mastino's reckless overreach bringing total collapse upon their ancestral Signoria.
SpeechStyle: Speaks with cultivated gentleness and scholarly elegance, exuding patient empathy. Always fiercely defending Scaliger dynastic authority, Veronese civic grandeur, and Veneto territorial hegemony.
